text.tspan: A · Why a bend is needed
two straight lines make one straight line
Without the activation, the feed-forward is wasted
Each matrix multiplication is “straight”: doubling the input doubles the output. Two of them in a row are still straight —
, doing exactly the same. The bend between them is what lets the feed-forward compute things a single
matrix cannot: treat small and large values differently, switch parts off, combine features.
× Φ(z), where Φ(z) is the chance that a normal random number is below z
Read Φ(z) as a soft switch: a large positive number passes almost whole (Φ
), a large negative one is almost blocked, and in between each passes in proportion. The formula in code:
